clue.text: Concerned with present line taken by newspaper that's unofficial

indicators.note: the newspaper's letters are taken into the run of other pieces, sitting between the first two

parts.note: of can mean about or concerning
here means present, in attendance
a cord is a line or string
FT is the Financial Times, the paper this puzzle appears in

explanation.surface: A newspaper's unofficial line on current affairs, given off the record.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper is the Financial Times, this puzzle's own paper, abbreviated as it usually is in FT crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Something said off the record is not for publication, so it is unofficial rather than formally stated.

clue.text: Dragon flying around you, ultimately aware of danger

indicators.note: the jumbled dragon letters go around the single letter from you
flying suggests the letters of dragon whirling into a new order
ultimately points to the final letter of you

explanation.surface: A dragon circles a person, who had better be alert to the danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges DRAGON to ONGARD, and 'around' wraps that round U, the last letter of 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on guard is to be watchful and alert for a threat, i.e. ready for danger.

clue.text: Note put on record in very serious manner

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece put on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
a tally is a running record or count

explanation.surface: A note is added to a file in a grave way.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatally describes something done with deadly or disastrous consequence, hence in a very serious manner.

clue.text: In on

definitions.meaning: second meaning: taking place, going on now

explanation.walkthrough: Two tiny prepositions look like nothing at all; each is a separate adjective sense of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening is slang for fashionable and lively, and it also means occurring at present.

clue.text: Instructions given as watch wound up

indicators.note: in a down entry, wound up means the letters climb, read from the bottom up

parts.note: a timer watches the clock, a stopwatch is a timer

explanation.surface: Instructions come with a watch that needs winding.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is a brief or set of terms given to someone, telling them what they are to do.

clue.text: Lock up prisoner very well

parts.note: con is slang for a convict
fine means very well, in good health or acceptably

explanation.surface: Lock up a prisoner who is in perfectly good health.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine is to shut someone in or restrict them, as a jailer locks up an inmate.

clue.text: Pattern of spinning pirouettes, ornate

indicators.note: spinning says the hidden letters are read backwards
of here means drawn out of, so the letters come from within the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dancer's spins form an elaborate pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hidden step no indicator; 'of', in the sense of taken out of, is the word that signals it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a rose-shaped decorative motif, a common pattern in architecture and design.

clue.text: Promising squeezes don't have enough pressure to make sausage

indicators.note: the promising word squeezes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: budding means promising, showing early talent
to lack is to not have enough of something
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A promising cook squeezes a sausage casing without enough force.
explanation.walkthrough: Black pudding is a British blood sausage, made with pig's blood and oats.
explanation.definitionFit: Black pudding is a kind of sausage made from blood, fat and cereal, cooked in a casing.

clue.text: Match finished, appear happy

parts.note: to match can mean to light, as one lights with a match
up means over, as in time's up

explanation.surface: The match over, someone looks pleased with the result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' reads as a sporting fixture, but it is the verb for striking a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: A face lights up when its owner becomes suddenly cheerful or delighted.

clue.text: Thinking it sad, men throwing a wobbly

indicators.note: throwing here means throwing out, discarding the letter a from the pool
wobbly signals the remaining letters shaking into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Men find it sad and throw a tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing a wobbly' is British for a tantrum, but here 'throwing' discards A and 'wobbly' rearranges ITSDMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a habitual way of thinking, an established set of attitudes.

clue.text: Clear format for cricket?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... vision is perfect, clear eyesight
second meaning: Twenty20 is the short form of cricket, twenty overs a side

explanation.walkthrough: Twenty20 is a short cricket format of twenty overs per team; 20/20 vision is normal sharp sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The same number pair names perfect eyesight and a short-match version of a bat-and-ball game.

clue.text: Drug — dope

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a ... is a fool, as in a proper ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' seems to repeat 'Drug', but it is the other sense, an idiot; a right charlie is British for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is street slang for cocaine and British slang for a silly person.

clue.text: Plant the aforementioned trees, like elms for starters

parts.note: this refers to something just mentioned

indicators.note: for starters takes the opening letter of each of the three following words

explanation.surface: Planting the trees just mentioned, elms for example.
explanation.definitionFit: The thistle is a prickly flowering plant, the emblem of Scotland.

clue.text: Fit of temper seeing place flooded?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for a tantrum
second meaning: a rice field kept under water

explanation.walkthrough: A paddy is British slang for a tantrum; the question mark covers describing a rice field as a flooded place.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a burst of anger and also a waterlogged field where rice grows.

clue.text: Credit claimed by eminent maverick for amount raised

indicators.note: the credit letters are claimed, taken inside, by the jumbled word
a maverick goes its own unorthodox way, so the letters of eminent are rearranged

parts.note: CR is the bookkeeping abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A distinguished rebel claims the credit for a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eminent maverick' looks like a celebrated rebel, but the adjective is the fodder and the noun the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An increment is an increase, especially a regular step up in salary.

clue.text: Converted, the cardinal having left home for place of worship

indicators.note: converted means changed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
having left says the letters for home are taken away from the pool

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A cardinal, newly converted, leaves home for church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' looks religious, but it rearranges THECARDAL, what is left of THE CARDINAL once IN goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is the principal church of a diocese, the seat of a bishop.

clue.text: Sort of clue, just perfect

parts.note: a down is a kind of crossword clue
right means just, fair

explanation.surface: A solver declares a clue simply perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' reads as merely, but it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect can mean utter or complete, as in a perfect stranger, which is what downright means.

clue.text: Get dancing bear for drinking establishment

parts.note: to win something is to get it

indicators.note: dancing moves the letters of bear about into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting a dancing bear to perform in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine bar is a place that sells wine and food for drinking on the premises.

clue.text: Marriage over by the look of it, stop talking

parts.note: a wedding ring stands for marriage
off means finished, called off

explanation.surface: A marriage looks finished, so the talking stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the look of it' admits that the ring only symbolises marriage; a ring taken off suggests one over.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring off is to end a telephone call by hanging up, so to stop talking.

clue.text: Lead and cobalt finally found

parts.note: the star is the lead in a play or film

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of cobalt

explanation.surface: Lead and cobalt have been discovered together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' and 'cobalt' look like a pair of metals, but lead is the leading role; 'found' is a verb meaning set up.
explanation.definitionFit: To found a business is to start it, to establish it from the beginning.

clue.text: Initially six below par in sport

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of six

parts.note: ailing means unwell, below par

explanation.surface: Six golfers under par at the start of a sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below par' sounds like good golf, but here it means feeling poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailing, racing boats under sail, is a sport with its own Olympic events.

clue.text: Insect tucking away green food

indicators.note: the insect tucks the green colour away inside itself

parts.note: an ant is an insect
lime is a shade of green

explanation.surface: An insect stashing away green food for later.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for nourishment, whatever feeds the body.

clue.text: Knock prize, first off

indicators.note: first off says the opening letter is removed

parts.note: winnings are what one wins, a prize

explanation.surface: Knocking a prize off its stand.
explanation.walkthrough: A knock is cricket slang for a batsman's innings, his turn at batting.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a knock is an informal word for a player's spell at the crease and the score made.

clue.text: Rice dish served in Ephesus, historically

indicators.note: served in says the dish is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A rice dish once served in the ancient city of Ephesus.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with fish or vegetables.

clue.text: Pile provided in English bones

indicators.note: in places the condition word inside the English bones

parts.note: bones is slang for dice
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A heap supplied in English bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pile' looks like a heap, but it means a large building; bones is old slang for dice.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile can be a large imposing building, and an edifice is exactly that.

clue.text: One looking down on others, giant knocked over primates

indicators.note: knocked over says the combined letters are turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a snob looks down on other people
big means giant

explanation.surface: A tall creature looking down on others knocks over some apes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One looking down on others' could be someone tall, but it is a snob.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibbons are small tree-dwelling apes, and apes belong to the primate order.

clue.text: Torn stocking design for clothing

indicators.note: stocking means holding in, so the torn word holds the design inside it

parts.note: rent is the past participle of rend, meaning torn
an aim is a design or purpose

explanation.surface: A ripped stocking pattern for an item of dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' looks like hosiery in the scene, but it means holding in stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for garments, what one wears.

clue.text: Indicator roads relatively empty?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a signal that indicates stop or go
second meaning: read as two words, light traffic means roads with few vehicles

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading, traffic that is light.
explanation.definitionFit: The signal at a junction directs vehicles, and the phrase read literally describes sparse motoring.
